newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans no cigarette excise tax rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans no cigarette excise tax rise in 1996.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry said on Thursday it would not increase excise tax for cigarettes this year.
"There are no plans to raise the excise tax for cigarettes in 1996," the ministry's press office said.
Western tobacco companies, which have invested heavily in Poland over the last twelve months, were concerned the tax might rise, forcing them to raise cigarette prices.
An increase of the tax in April pushed cigarette prices up by between three and five percent.

Poland's lucrative tobacco market, where some 100 billion cigarettes are smoked each year, has lured such investors as Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, Seita, British American Tobacco Industries Plc (B.A.T.) and Germany's Reemtsma.
Poland's tobacco excise tax is now between 40.3 zloty and 58.3 zloyts per 1,000 cigarettes, depending on their type.
